inputs.name: events per genome per generation
inputs.cite: evo008@L90 (Duffy, relayed); M-108 for u and its meaning

wd.reading: only 1.09% of the neutral substitutions land in the divergent sites, so the prediction to set against them is 169,344
wd.holds: the arithmetic reproduces exactly (15,482,880 x 35e6/3.2e9); his first correction (38.4) is not used in it (84,672 with it)

day.reading: the neutral expectation applies to the entire genome (evo009@L58); Hancock put all of it on the 1.09%
day.holds: the whole-genome reading is the one Hancock also states; Day does not restate 169,344 in evo009

critic.reading: which sites fix is random; the 1.09% marks recency, not the only sites that could fix (Hancock, evo009@L57)
critic.holds: the 35M are the realised substitutions, so the whole-genome count is their comparator: 30.97M at 201,600 or 38.71M at 252,000 (0.88x, 1.11x of 35M); WD's scaling predicts 169,344 divergent sites against 35M observed (1/207)

notes: Arithmetic as printed holds. The object is which sites the expectation applies to: multiplying the expected count by the share of sites that turned out divergent counts the predicted substitutions that would hit a site set fixed in advance; the divergent set is not fixed in advance but is the realised substitutions, so both Hancock and Day (evo009) apply the expectation to the whole genome. Whether 76.8 is a haploid events rate or the diploid SNV product (and so one lineage or two) is M-108; the d = 0.80 input is M-110. The 35M includes polymorphism (CSAC, one genome per species).
